claims.text: Pressure-robust superconductivity in the HEA is governed by the stability of its disordered bcc structure.
High configurational entropy maintains the bcc structure under high pressure.
Stability of the bcc structure minimizes pressure-induced lattice distortions.
Structural stability under pressure preserves the electronic density of states.
Structural stability under pressure preserves electron-phonon coupling and pairing.
Preservation of electronic structure and electron-phonon pairing makes superconductivity less pressure-sensitive or enhances it under compression.
(TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 has a bcc crystal structure at ambient pressure.
Superconductivity in the Ti-Zr-Hf-Nb-Ta HEA system remains robust up to approximately 200 GPa.
The disordered bcc lattice remains intact under significant pressure-induced compression.
With increasing pressure, the HEA will maintain or modestly increase its Tc.
Pure Nb and Ta are expected to exhibit decreasing Tc under the same pressure conditions.
Conventional binary superconductors typically exhibit decreasing Tc under pressure.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the HEA retains its disordered bcc structure without a pressure-induced phase transition.
A pressure-induced loss of structural integrity would compromise the proposed governing mechanism.
In CsCl-type tellurides, the HEA AgInSnPbBiTe5 has nearly pressure-independent Tc from 13.0 to 35.1 GPa, whereas PbTe has decreasing Tc.
Prior telluride results link pressure robustness of superconductivity to configurational entropy of mixing.
The similarity between the telluride and Ti-Zr-Hf-Nb-Ta observations suggests that HEA effects generally enhance pressure robustness of superconductivity.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the mechanism is only expected to apply while the bcc structure is retained, but the falsification rule treats loss of the bcc structure as falsification. A phase transition instead places the experiment outside the stated domain and does not by itself refute the conditional mechanism.
The baseline is described as binary superconductors or dilution alloys, but the stated examples, pure Nb and pure Ta, are elemental superconductors rather than binaries or dilution alloys.
